sections.title: Identify the following sentences as True or False.

The robes of the new-born child are as white as a cloud.

The funeral shroud is white as a feather and white as a cloud.

sections.title: Answer in one or two sentences (about 30 words).

questions.q: For whom do the weavers weave at break of day and in the moonlight chill?
questions.answer: At break of day they weave robes for a new-born child; in the moonlight chill they weave a funeral shroud for a dead man.

questions.q: What are the weavers weaving at break of day?
questions.answer: They are weaving the bright blue robes of a new-born child, blue as the wing of a wild halcyon.

questions.q: What is the similarity between 'break of day' and 'a new-born child'?
questions.answer: Both stand for a beginning: dawn is the beginning of the day and birth is the beginning of life; both are fresh and full of hope.

questions.q: Why are the weavers 'solemn and still' at night?
questions.answer: They are weaving a funeral shroud for a dead man; death is a sad, serious occasion, so their mood is quiet and solemn.

questions.q: What three stages of life are shown in the poem?
questions.answer: Birth (robes of a new-born child), youth/marriage (marriage veils of a queen) and death (a dead man's funeral shroud).

questions.q: How does the poet link the time of day, colour and occasion in 'Indian Weavers'?
questions.answer: At break of day (beginning) the weavers weave blue robes for a new-born child (birth). At fall of night they weave bright purple and green marriage veils for a queen (youth and joy). In the moonlight chill they weave a white funeral shroud (death). Time, colour and mood together show the cycle of life.

or.q: Pick out the similes in 'Indian Weavers' and explain any two.
or.answer: 'Blue as the wing of halcyon wild', 'like the plumes of a peacock, purple and green', 'white as a feather and white as a cloud'. The first compares the child's robe to the bright blue kingfisher's wing, suggesting freshness; the last compares the shroud's whiteness to a feather and a cloud, suggesting peace, purity and lightness of the departing soul.
